cards.explanation: The answer is that they confess their sins and their fathers' sins. Verse 2 says they "…stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers." They didn't only own up to their own sins, they owned up to their fathers' iniquities too. That takes some humility, friends, and I know how hard that is when it's your own mess to admit.

The answer is to bless the LORD their God. The Levites say, "Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting…" It's a call to praise before they say anything else. I like that they start with who God is.

The answer is with God creating the heavens and the earth. They go all the way back to the beginning. The Levites pray, "You created the heavens, the highest heavens with all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them." They didn't start with their own troubles, friends. They started with who made everything.

The answer is Abraham. Verse 7 says God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans "…and gave him the name Abraham." The Levites remember that God picked him and named him. That's a big moment to bring up in a prayer.

The answer is True. Verse 8 says God made a covenant with Abraham "…to give it to his descendants." Then the Levites say, "You have kept Your promise, because You are righteous." They're standing there in hard times and still saying God keeps His word. That's the kind of memory worth holding onto.

The answer is that they acted with arrogance against Israel's fathers. The signs and wonders came "…for You knew they had acted with arrogance against our fathers." The Levites also say God made a name for Himself that endures to this day.

The answer is fire. Verse 12 says God led them "…with a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way in which they should travel." The cloud covered the day and the fire covered the night. I'd have been happy with a nightlight, friends.

The answer is True. Verse 14 says, "You revealed to them Your holy Sabbath and gave them commandments and statutes and laws through Your servant Moses." Moses was Israel's leader, and the Sabbath came to them along with the laws. The Levites remember it as something God revealed.

The answer is rock. Verse 15 says, "In their hunger You gave them bread from heaven; in their thirst You brought them water from the rock." Water out of a rock, friends. I've squeezed a lot of things, but never that.
The answer is False. Verse 15 says God "…told them to go in and possess the land that You had sworn to give them." Nobody was told to stay put. God sent them toward what He had promised.

The answer is to take them back to slavery in Egypt, and it's a hard one to read. Verse 17 says they "…appointed a leader to return them to their bondage in Egypt." After everything God did to bring them out, they picked someone to lead them back. The very next line is that God did not forsake them.

The answer is anger. Verse 17 says, "But You are a forgiving God, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in loving devotion, and You did not forsake them." Read that one slowly, friends, because it's the center of the whole prayer. It comes right after the people stiffened their necks and appointed a leader to return them to their bondage in Egypt.

The answer is True. Verse 19 says that even then, "…the pillar of cloud never turned away from guiding them on their path…" The calf was right there in verse 18, with terrible blasphemies, and still the cloud kept leading. The prayer says God did not forsake them in the wilderness.

The answer is that they did not wear out. Verse 21 says, "For forty years You sustained them in the wilderness, so that they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell." Forty years of walking, and the clothes held up. I can't get a pair of socks to last a winter, friends.

The answer is stars. Verse 23 says God "…multiplied their descendants like the stars of heaven…" Funny thing, I get a star in my sky for every finished cookie box. Theirs came from God multiplying them.

The answer is False. Verse 24 says their descendants "…went in and possessed the land; You subdued before them the Canaanites dwelling in the land." Nobody drove them back out. The promise from verse 8 was coming true right there.

The answer is houses full of goods and wells already dug. Verse 25 says they took "…houses full of all goods, wells already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance." Houses already stocked and wells already dug. That's moving into a kitchen where somebody already preheated the oven.

The answer is that they kill the prophets, and it's a heavy line. Verse 26 says, "They killed Your prophets, who had admonished them to return to You." The prophets had been urging them to come back. I think that one hurts to say out loud.

The answer is False. Verse 28 says, "But as soon as they had rest, they again did evil in Your sight." Then when they cried out again, God "…heard from heaven, and You delivered them many times in Your compassion." The Levites don't hide the cycle, friends, and they don't hide God's compassion either.

The answer is that He is a gracious and compassionate God. That's the reason the Levites give. Verse 31 says, "But in Your great compassion, You did not put an end to them; nor did You forsake them, for You are a gracious and compassionate God." The reason is who God is, not anything they did. I'm glad about that.

The answer is False. In verse 33 the Levites say, "You are just in all that has befallen us, because You have acted faithfully, while we have acted wickedly." They call God just and faithful, and they own their part.

The answer is in the land God gave their fathers. Verse 36 says, "So here we are today as slaves in the land You gave our fathers to enjoy its fruit and goodness…" They say it twice, "…here we are as slaves!" Slaves in the very land that was promised to them.
The answer is kings. Verse 37 says, "Its abundant harvest goes to the kings You have set over us because of our sins." The people go on to say, "We are in great distress."

The answer is that they make a binding agreement in writing. Verse 38 says, "In view of all this, we make a binding agreement, putting it in writing and sealing it with the names of our leaders, Levites, and priests." After all that history, they put it in writing and sealed it. A prayer was spoken, and now the names go into the agreement. The story isn't over, friends.
